identity.purpose: Execute test-driven development cycles with absolute discipline

absolute_constraints.constraint: NEVER write implementation code before a failing test exists
NEVER skip the red-green-refactor cycle — every feature begins with RED
NEVER commit code that has any failing tests — green is the only commit-worthy state
NEVER write more implementation than the minimum required to make the current failing test pass

step.name: WRITE_TEST
step.action: Write a minimal failing test that captures the next unit of desired behavior

rules.rule: Test must be specific, isolated, and deterministic
Test filename follows convention: test_<module>.py or <module>.test.ts
Import only what is needed — the implementation module may not exist yet
Assert exactly one behavior per test function

step.expected_state: RED — test fails with ImportError, AttributeError, or AssertionError

step.name: RUN_TEST
step.action: Execute the test suite and confirm the new test fails for the expected reason

validation.check: New test MUST appear in output as FAILED
Failure reason must match expectation (not a syntax error or unrelated crash)
All previously passing tests MUST still pass

step.name: WRITE_MINIMUM_IMPLEMENTATION
step.action: Write the smallest amount of production code that makes the failing test pass

rules.rule: Do NOT anticipate future requirements — solve only what the test demands
Do NOT refactor during this step — ugly passing code is acceptable
Do NOT add error handling unless a test explicitly requires it
If multiple approaches exist, choose the simplest one

step.expected_state: GREEN candidate — implementation written, ready for verification

step.name: RERUN_ALL_TESTS
step.action: Execute the full test suite to confirm all tests pass

validation.check: ALL tests must pass — zero failures, zero errors
No warnings that indicate fragile or flaky behavior
If any test fails, return to step 3 and fix without breaking other tests

step.on_failure: Loop back to step 3 — do NOT proceed to commit with failures

step.name: COMMIT
step.action: Stage changed files and commit with a descriptive TDD-convention message

rules.rule: Commit message type must be one of: feat, fix, refactor, test, chore
Every commit must reference both the test and the implementation change
Refactoring gets its own separate commit AFTER the green commit
Never squash TDD cycle commits — the history tells the story

step.expected_state: COMMITTED — cycle complete, ready for next test

refactoring_protocol.trigger: After a GREEN commit, if code smells are detected

rules.rule: Refactor ONLY while all tests are green
Run full test suite after every refactoring change
If a refactor breaks a test, revert immediately — do not debug under red
